findings.text: This dossier exposes operations to configure, query and probe the virtual performance monitor through a device attribute style interface plus a helper reporting the host version ceiling. Configuration covers interrupt selection, event filtering, backing choice, counter count and final initialization, query returns the interrupt, and probing reports support for the five configuration selectors.

Steal time handling is exposed for setting, retrieving and probing a single guest address attribute. Setting records the address once after validation, retrieval returns the stored value, and probing reports availability from host support.

The architecture layer exposes dispatchers for device attributes, virtual CPU event exchange, the main virtual CPU control entry and register enumeration. Attribute dispatch fans out by functional group, event exchange separates retrieval from installation, the control entry multiplexes lifecycle and register and attribute and event operations, and enumeration reports the total register count.

The virtual CPU control entry receives a file context plus operation code and user pointer. It supports initialization with a copied descriptor, single register access gated on initialization and ordered after any pending reset, register list query with two stage sizing, attribute set and query and probe via copied descriptors, event retrieval and installation gated on initialization, and finalization with a user supplied selector, rejecting unknown codes.

Attribute operations route solely on a group selector toward performance monitor, timer or steal time back ends, with any other group reported as unsupported. A thin outer layer unconditionally forwards to the architecture dispatcher, which performs the group selection for set, query and probe paths.

Event retrieval clears the caller structure before filling, while event installation rejects any nonzero reserved or padding elements before delegating to the architecture implementation. Both directions require an initialized virtual CPU at the control layer.

Nested control translation invalidations apply only when the virtual machine advertises a specific nested virtualization feature, otherwise the range operation returns without effect. The whole space variant covers from zero up to two raised to the address size held in the stage two table descriptor, and skips work when that descriptor is absent to tolerate teardown races.

Range invalidation walks every virtual CPU and considers only entries whose cached translation pointer exists and is marked valid. An entry is discarded when its translated region, derived from its page size exponent and table level and aligned to its own size, overlaps the requested interval treated as start inclusive to end exclusive.

Level encodings combine a two bit level with a two bit granule selector. The mapping yields no size for level zero in all granules and for level one except the smallest granule, one gigabyte for smallest granule level one, two megabytes, four kilobytes, thirty two megabytes, sixteen kilobytes, five hundred twelve megabytes and sixty four kilobytes for the remaining defined combinations, with unknown selectors yielding zero and the public wrapper substituting one gigabyte for zero.

Page size exponents twelve, fourteen and sixteen map to the four, sixteen and sixty four kilobyte granule selectors respectively, combined with the low two bits of the table level. A negative level bypasses the table and yields the zero encoding that later maps to the maximum size fallback.

The overflow interrupt may be a private or shared peripheral interrupt that passes a global consistency check. On one interrupt controller generation the value must equal a single architected number, otherwise private values must agree across all virtual CPUs while shared values must differ across virtual CPUs.

Event filtering validates that the requested interval lies within the host supported event count and that the action is allow or deny, rejects changes after the virtual machine has run, requires a selected backing monitor, lazily allocates a per virtual machine bitmap whose initial contents are the opposite of the first applied action, then sets bits for allow ranges and clears bits for deny ranges.

Backing monitor selection searches a global list by type identifier, rejects selection after the virtual machine has run or when a filter already exists for a different monitor, then records the monitor, copies its supported processor mask and optionally snapshots a slot count field when strict virtualization is requested. Counter count selection requires an existing monitor and a value within the host maximum.

The reported performance monitor version ceiling derives from the sanitized debug feature register, except that a system workaround for implementation defined trapping forces an implementation defined version, a raw implementation defined value is treated as zero, and any other value is capped at version three point five.

The steal time base may be programmed only once from its invalid sentinel to a sixty four byte aligned guest address that resolves to a valid host address in a memory slot. Reprogramming is rejected as already existing, and retrieval returns the current stored value even if still invalid.

Core register enumeration walks the fixed general plus floating point state in units of thirty two bit words, assigning eight byte size to general registers and stack and program counter and state and selected system registers, sixteen byte size to vector registers and four byte size to floating point status and control, skipping unaligned accesses and skipping vector registers through this path when scalable vector extension is enabled.

Scalable vector register count is zero without that feature, otherwise it equals the slice count multiplied by the sum of predicate and data registers plus a single terminator register, plus one more selector for vector lengths. The current slice count is constantly one.

Fault reporting indicates system error syndrome availability from a hardware capability and pending status from either a virtualization control bit or a nested pending flag, supplying a syndrome value only when both pending and availability hold, and never reporting a pending external data abort because that condition is delivered synchronously during installation.
Total register count is the sum of core, scalable vector, system and firmware pseudo register contributions.

Nested control translation invalidation and whole space invalidation both require the virtual machine memory management lock held in write mode, as asserted on entry. The whole space variant tolerates the table pointer becoming null under that lock as a sign of concurrent teardown.

Performance monitor configuration requires the per virtual machine configuration lock held across the operation, asserted inside the monitor handler and acquired by the architecture attribute dispatcher around that handler and also held during backing monitor selection.

Backing monitor list traversal is protected by a global monitor list mutex held only for the duration of the search and update, while steal time address validation uses a short source read critical section around the host address lookup without holding it across the final store.

The cached nested control translation entry carries a validity flag, a write physical address used for overlap testing, a page size exponent and table level used to derive region size, plus an unmapping handle released on invalidation. A per virtual machine counter tracks how many such entries are currently valid and is decremented on each discard.

Per virtual CPU monitor state includes a creation flag, an interrupt number with an initialization predicate, and an overflow notification work item. Per virtual machine monitor state includes a backing monitor pointer, an event filter bitmap and a supported processor mask plus a slot snapshot. Per virtual CPU steal state is a single base address with a defined invalid sentinel.

Core register identifiers combine a fixed architecture and core category prefix with a word offset and a size suffix distinguishing four, eight and sixteen byte accesses. Enumeration order follows increasing word offset over the combined general and floating point area.

Monitor lifecycle moves from absent to configurable when the virtual CPU has the feature, remains configurable across interrupt and filter and backing and count selections until final initialization, then becomes created and rejects further configuration as busy. Filter allocation moves from absent to present with polarity fixed by the first action, and initialization without an explicit interrupt on the newest controller generation moves to a default architected interrupt.

Exception installation moves from requested to committed by synchronously injecting an external abort when asked and then injecting a system error when pending, clearing emulation state and adjusting the program counter whenever a pending exception flag was set. Retrieval does not change state and never shows the already committed abort as pending.

Register list query moves from size discovery to bulk copy, reporting the total count first and requiring the caller supplied capacity to cover it before copying indices, otherwise signaling insufficient space.

Invalidating an entry already marked invalid triggers a fatal assertion, supplying an unsupported page size exponent triggers a fatal trap, enumerating scalable vector registers before finalization emits a developer warning, and enumerating core registers with an unexpected size also warns. Page table teardown racing whole space invalidation is tolerated by a null check.

User memory accesses for attribute payloads and control descriptors can fail and are reported as faults without side effects, interrupt selection without an in kernel controller and monitor initialization without an initialized controller are rejected, and steal time programming validates alignment and memory slot membership to avoid recording an unusable address.

System error installation validates platform syndrome support and masks reserved syndrome bits, rejecting unsupported combinations, and control layer installation rejects any nonzero reserved or padding fields to preserve forward compatibility.

Attribute groups distinguish performance monitor, timer and steal time control, monitor attributes distinguish interrupt, event filter, backing selection, counter count and initialization, and steal time uses a single address attribute. Presence probing succeeds only for these selectors when the corresponding feature is available.

Translation size constants used by the level mapping are one gigabyte, two megabytes, four kilobytes, thirty two megabytes, sixteen kilobytes, five hundred twelve megabytes and sixty four kilobytes, page exponents are twelve, fourteen and sixteen, steal time alignment is sixty four bytes, and scalable vector enumeration distinguishes predicate, data, terminator and length selectors.

Virtual CPU control operations include initialization, single register access, register list query, attribute set and query and probe, event retrieval and installation, and finalization. Register access and event operations require prior initialization, and list query additionally requires finalization.
